claims.text: Adding a minor amount of silver to the HEA will reduce both coefficient of friction and wear rate over a wide service-temperature range.
Silver addition will promote in-situ formation of a lubricious, silver-rich surface film.
The proposed intervention is addition of 1–2 at% silver during alloy synthesis.
Room temperature to approximately 600°C represents the proposed broad test and service-temperature range.
Silver will segregate to the alloy surface during sliding service.
Surface-segregated silver will form a continuous or patchy silver-rich tribolayer.
The silver-rich surface phase will be lubricious and reduce interfacial shear forces.
The protective silver-rich layer will mitigate abrasive and adhesive wear.
The silver-rich layer will maintain structural integrity across the proposed temperature range.
Silver doping is expected to reduce both coefficient of friction and wear rate by approximately 20–30% relative to the undoped alloy.
The anticipated 20–30% reductions are based on analogous systems.
The intervention should remain effective if silver segregates without significant evaporation or coarsening at elevated temperature.
The lubricating effect may be compromised if silver fails to form a coherent tribolayer.
The proposed comparison uses undoped and 1–2 at% silver-doped samples tested under identical loads from room temperature to 600°C.
XPS and TEM will be used to assess silver segregation and tribolayer integrity after testing.

The hypothesis will be rejected if the doped samples fail to show statistically significant reductions in both friction and wear across the entire tested range, or if no silver-rich tribolayer is observed.
